chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: How Cab Calloway got the Cotton Club job
summary: With Ellington away filming, Duke recommended Calloway; gangsters Owney Madden and Herman Stark forced the Savoy manager to release his contract and turned the Missourians into Calloway's band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: In those days. I'm going back before 1930, around that time, because Calloway didn't get his band till '30, really.
And that's when he got his band. When Duke went to make Check and Doublecheck with Amos and Andy, the picture, Check and Doublecheck, --

-- they didn't have nobody to come in the Cotton Club to take Duke Ellington's place. So Duke Ellington told Herman Stark and Owrey Madden to go over and hear this kid over at the Savoy Ballroom, "He's a good entertainer. He looks good. He's got a nice personality. And I think he could do something with it."
That's right, and I can tell it because I think all the people implicated are dead now anyway.
So, anyway, they went over and saw Calloway and they liked what they saw and they told Owrey Madden, "We want his contract. Now you give us his contract or else we'll blow up the Savoy Ballroom."
Oh, yeah. These were the real boys in those days and when they said something, you did it.
Oh. Owey Madden was as powerful in Harlem just like Al Capone was in the south side Chicago.
That's the way Al Capone -- I mean, that's the way Owey Madden was in Harlem, you see.

And Bo Gill tore up that contract and Herman Stark and Owey Madden took Calloway and put him in the Cotton Club. And the band was a cooperative band and they took the band away from the boys and give it to Calloway and said, 'This is your band.' And they got him signed up --
take the Missourians to Cab Calloway's band.

-- Irving Mills signed him because Irving Mills had every band in the Cotton Club. They signed Calloway up, put him on the air and made a little club -- I forget. If you could call in a name, you could get so many records. It was a real long name. I forget what it was right now. But he made --
He made 'St. James Infirmary'. And they created -- for the Cotton Club show they created Minnie the
And from then on, shew, Calloway was gone.
That's right, and he, all the guys in the band, he started to firing different guys in the band from the Missourians -- he was always trying to improve his band. You have to give him that.
Because now there's no more cooperation.
